problem: The first carry equation is mislabelled. The text says 'L means Aout = Gin + Ein·Ai·Bi′', but the correct equation is Gout = Gin + Ein·Ai·Bi′. Gout is never defined, and L is not defined as A<B.
fix: Define G as A>B so far and L as A<B so far. Write Gout = Gin + Ein·Ai·Bi′; Lout = Lin + Ein·Ai′·Bi; Eout = Ein·(Ai XNOR Bi).

problem: The final sentence says 'Lout=1 means Aout=1 means A=B', which is wrong. Lout=1 means A<B; Eout=1 means A=B.
fix: After the last cell, Gout=1 means A>B, Lout=1 means A<B, and Eout=1 means A=B.

problem: The figure says the same three inputs feed a 3-to-8 decoder, an 8-to-1 multiplexer and a 4-bit comparator. An 8:1 mux needs 8 data inputs plus 3 selects, and a 4-bit comparator needs two 4-bit words (8 bits), so the same three bits cannot feed all three.
fix: Show the decoder and mux sharing A, B, C only as select/address bits, give the mux its 8 data inputs, and give the comparator two separate 4-bit words. Do not claim the same three bits feed all three blocks.

problem: A linear AND chain for n bit-equality signals needs n−1 AND gates, not n, and the XNOR delay is omitted from the chain comparison. The delay is tXNOR + (n−1)·tAND, or n·tAND only as a loose upper bound.
fix: State the chain delay as tXNOR + (n−1)·tAND and compare it with the balanced-tree delay tXNOR + ceil(log₂n)·tAND.

problem: The delay is written as log₂N mux levels for an N:1 mux. For N not a power of two this is not an integer; a mux tree uses ceil(log₂N) levels.
fix: Write tpd ≈ ceil(log₂N) × tmux for a general N:1 mux tree.
